name: monday.com
subcategory: team projects, issues and delivery planning
tagline: Configure boards, fields, views, and automations for one team's workflow

pricing.notes: Official Basic monthly seat price; minimum seat counts can apply.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 2 seats, 3 boards, 3 docs, 200 items initially (referrals can raise this to 1,000), 500 MB storage; no automations/integrations

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited items/viewers, 5 GB storage and 1,000 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 3 workflows, 250 automation actions/month, 250 integration actions/month, 1,000 API calls/day and 2,000 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 20 workflows, 25,000 automation + 25,000 integration actions/month, 10,000 API calls/day, 3,000 AI credits/month and 100 GB storage

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 250 workflows, up to 250,000 automation + 250,000 integration actions/month, 25,000 API calls/day and custom AI credits

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2 seats, 3 boards, 3 docs, 200 items initially (up to 1,000 through referrals), 500 MB storage, and no automations/integrations
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (about 18% off); 14-day trial, no card
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid plans start at 3 seats and then use seat buckets (3, 5, 10, etc.), so small teams can pay for unused seats. On Standard, the first 3 guests are free and each further block of 4 guests counts as 1 billed seat. New customers after 2026-05-06 may face a required AI-credit purchase during setup, and extra AI-credit top-ups use dynamic pricing.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For monday.com, configure boards, fields, views, and automations for one team's workflow. The hard boundary is flexible data model, integrations, templates, dashboards, and enterprise governance, plus collaboration, integrations, and organizational trust.
coreLoopDIY: Plan and track a small team's work through configurable boards, fields, views, and simple automations, with milestones, comments, and a searchable activity history.
whatYouLose: flexible data model, integrations, templates, dashboards, and enterprise governance
ongoingBurden: auth, permissions, notifications, search, migrations, audit history, integrations, backups, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for monday.com because teams pay because project state has to remain authoritative through staff changes, outages, and years of accumulated workflow exceptions. The recurring cost buys auth, permissions, notifications, search, migrations, audit history, integrations, backups, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a small-team tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for monday.com in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: plan and track a small team's work through configurable boards, fields, views, and simple automations, with milestones, comments, and a searchable activity history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement organizations, projects, members, issues, labels, cycles, and milestones.
Provide list, kanban, and simple timeline views backed by one canonical issue model.
Add comments, mentions, assignments, watchers, and a complete activity log.
Implement project roles for owner, member, and viewer and test every mutation.
Add search, CSV import or export, email notifications, and daily database backups.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, migrations, seed data, and an admin recovery command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of external integrations.
Deliberately leave out enterprise portfolio planning and SSO.
Deliberately leave out native mobile clients and vendor-operated uptime.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
